title: Optimizers: Momentum, Adam & Learning-Rate Schedules
summary: Why plain gradient descent struggles on ill-conditioned losses and how momentum, RMSProp, bias-corrected Adam, AdamW's decoupled weight decay and warmup-plus-cosine schedules each fix part of the problem.
takeaways: Momentum averages gradients over time: oscillations cancel and consistent directions build up speed.
Adam divides by a running RMS of each coordinate's gradient. Bias correction makes the first step exactly lr·sign(g).
For Adam, L2 in the gradient and decoupled weight decay differ. AdamW shrinks the weights directly.
Warm up linearly, then decay along a cosine. Check the boundary steps for off-by-one errors.

steps.label: Schedule
steps.detail: lr = warmup/cosine(step), set before the update.

steps.label: Decay
steps.detail: p -= lr·λ·p, directly on the weights and not through g.

steps.label: Moments
steps.detail: m = β₁m + (1 − β₁)g and v = β₂v + (1 − β₂)g², kept per parameter.

steps.label: Bias-correct
steps.detail: m̂ = m/(1 − β₁ᵗ), v̂ = v/(1 − β₂ᵗ), with t counted from 1.

terms.definition: A velocity v = μv + g that accumulates past gradients; the parameter steps along v instead of g.
Adaptive moment estimation: momentum divided by the running RMS of gradients, with bias correction for the zero initialisation.
Dividing the moment estimates by 1 − βᵗ so their expected value isn't pulled towards zero early in training.
Shrinking weights by lr·λ·p separately from the gradient-based update, as in AdamW.
Linearly increasing the learning rate from 0 over the first steps, before the main schedule takes over.
lr = min + ½(base − min)(1 + cos(π·progress)), a smooth decay from base to min.
